before.name: Shabareesh Parlakota
before.feedback: The travel positioning and visual presentation are considered, and the preference form is clear. I could not complete native date entry reliably in this review environment, so I am leaving execution unscored rather than calling the app broken. A sample generated itinerary would make the core experience easier to assess.
before.tested: Landing, destination autocomplete Japan, India origin, traveller type/count and budget controls. Date fills changed DOM values but did not reliably update the form; Continue remained disabled.
before.limitations: Native date control/tooling limitation prevented reaching itinerary generation. No booking or payment attempted.

after.name: Shabareesh Parlakota
after.feedback: The considered visual design carries through to a tailored five-day itinerary, and activity alternatives and saved changes work. Tighten budget enforcement and recalculation: a ₹2 lakh ceiling produced a ₹2.15 lakh estimate, and swapping a ₹7,500-per-person transfer for a ₹3,500 alternative left the total unchanged.
after.tested: Chrome second pass resolved native dates with textbox.pressSequentially, using01–05Oct2026, India→Japan,2friends, Comfortable budget, slow pace/quiet nightlife, vegetarian/no-alcohol notes and INR200000 ceiling. Generated tailored Tokyo+Fuji five-day itinerary with airport transport. Swapped first transfer to Narita Express ₹3500/person and verified replacement survived reload. Initial estimated total₹215000 stayed unchanged after cheaper swap.
after.limitations: Earlier date-entry failure was browser tooling, not an app defect. Live prices, travel times, venue availability, vegetarian-menu accuracy and entry requirements not independently verified. Regenerate-day and new-trip reset not exercised; no booking/payment. Evidence stored under evidence-095-104/027-*.

before.name: Ashray
tested: Inspected seven existing decisions and confidence/calibration metrics
Filled synthetic title, reasoning, category and revisit date; Save remained disabled
Retried date entry and blur; new entry was not created; reload returned existing seven logs
limitations: Date control did not commit a usable value during browser testing; cannot separate app validation from browser automation limitation
Existing decisions/outcomes were not changed; new-entry persistence unverified
before.feedback: The decision, reflection and calibration model is thoughtful, and outcome filters make the existing history useful. I could not verify creation because the native date input did not commit during automated testing; functionality and overall scores are withheld rather than treating this as an app defect.

after.name: Ashray
tested: Second pass resolved native date entry using visible Chrome keyboard actions, with synthetic revisit date 2026-09-01.
Created QA Demo: Try a 20-minute study block with reasoning and confidence 3; total increased from 7 to 8 and new record persisted after reload.
Recorded Mixed outcome and a synthetic reflection on only the new test record; metrics became 8 logged, 7 resolved, 2 correct, 2 mixed, 3 wrong, 1 pending and 43% hit rate.
Reload preserved the outcome and reflection; search for QA Demo isolated the new record.
Inspected single-page metrics, category/calibration controls and expanded resolved record visually.
limitations: Earlier native date block was browser tooling; no deduction for that limitation.
Existing seeded records were not modified.
No edit, reopen or undo control was visible on the resolved test record; reminders and long-term calibration were not verified.
after.feedback: The decision-to-reflection loop works end to end, and both the saved outcome and calibration totals survive reload. Add a clear correction flow for entered decisions or outcomes and explain how small sample sizes affect the calibration percentages.

before.name: Uttiya Biswas
before.feedback: The wellness onboarding has a calm visual hierarchy and an explicit demo entry. Native cycle-date entry could not be completed through the review tool, so the tracking features remain unverified; provide a skip path or preconfigured demo for assessment.
before.tested: Demo credentials entry, sign in, fictional first-name onboarding, date step and reload.
before.limitations: Review-tool limitation at native date input; core wellness screens inaccessible beyond onboarding. No real health data used.

after.name: Uttiya Biswas
tested: Second pass used the offered demo login and synthetic onboarding name QA Demo, last period 2026-08-15, default 28-day cycle; visible keyboard entry resolved native date tooling.
Onboarding completed and home dashboard showed personalized cycle phase and expected next period; identity and cycle setup survived reloads.
LOG YOUR SYMPTOMS crashed to a blank screen; browser error ReferenceError: moodRating is not defined.
After separate reloads, Calendar, Learn and Relief each crashed to blank screens. Browser errors named periodDates, readingSessions and triedMethods respectively.
Profile rendered name, cycle values, settings/help affordances and a medical disclaimer. Its fixed Tracking since Jan 2024 text did not correspond to new synthetic onboarding.
Inspected dashboard and failure screenshots; all main navigation destinations were attempted.
limitations: Earlier native date block was a tooling limitation and is not penalized.
Only synthetic demo data used; no real medical data, notifications or device permissions were entered or granted.
Clinical correctness, security claims and real account persistence were not assessed.
Symptom tracking and three main sections could not be used due confirmed runtime crashes; deeper profile settings were not exercised.
after.feedback: The onboarding and home dashboard provide a clear, visually consistent starting point, and the cycle setup survives reload. Fix the runtime crashes in symptom logging, Calendar, Learn and Relief before adding more features, then verify that a saved symptom can be revisited across sessions.

before.name: Bhagyam Maheshwary
before.feedback: The urgency ordering and compact summary make the food-waste problem easy to understand. Native date entry could not be completed through the review tool, so adding food, consumption and saved totals remain unverified; a sample-item demo would allow the full workflow to be assessed.
before.tested: Dashboard, Add Food synthetic name/date, retry with blur, validation response and reload.
before.limitations: Review-tool limitation: native date fill changed the visible value without the application accepting it. Existing foods untouched; core save/consume/persistence unobservable.

after.name: Bhagyam Maheshwary
after.feedback: The urgency ordering and compact summary make the food-waste problem easy to act on, and adding and consuming an item updates the correct totals across reloads. Add a visible consumption history and an undo option so accidental taps can be corrected and users can review what they saved.
after.tested: Second pass resolved native expiry entry with keyboard input. Added QA Demo Milk expiring1Sep2026: items8→9 and expiringsoon2→3; reload retained item. Marked only that synthetic item consumed: totals returned8/2 and consumedthisweek0→1, retained after reload.
after.limitations: Earlier date issue was browser tooling, not an app defect. Existing foods untouched; notifications, across-week aggregation and deletion recovery not verified. No consumption history/undo visible in reviewed single-dashboard flow.

before.feedback: The sample-room flow reaches a comparison screen with furniture hotspots, but the hero text is almost white on white and the saved render disappeared on reload. Improve contrast and persistence, then replace generic retailer-homepage links and preset imagery with verifiable room-specific results and product destinations.

after.feedback: The sample-room flow reaches a comparison screen with furniture hotspots, but the hero text is almost white on white and the saved render disappeared on reload. Improve contrast and persistence, replace generic retailer-homepage links with actual product destinations, and demonstrate room-specific generation from a fresh uploaded image.

before.feedback: The five-step quiz, product swaps and saved routine are clear and work. But the core budget promise fails: selecting under ₹1,000 produced a ₹3,514 routine, with no explanation of monthly cost versus purchase cost. I expected the recommendations to respect the answers, not just repeat them in the heading.

after.feedback: The quiz, product swaps, saved routine and context-aware chat form a coherent experience, and the routine survives reload. But selecting under ₹1,000 returned routines costing over ₹3,500, with the moisturiser counted twice. I expected the recommendations to respect the budget and explain upfront cost versus monthly replenishment.

before.feedback: The take-home earnings model is well chosen, with useful cost, waiting-time, platform comparison, and history views; the saved rider preference survived reload. Improve incomplete-input handling—the form displayed ₹5,000/hour before valid times existed—and make the AI analysis resolve reliably instead of leaving the user in an analyzing state.

after.feedback: The gig-worker focus is well developed: fuel, maintenance and waiting time feed clear take-home calculations, and preferences survive reload. Avoid displaying thousands of rupees per hour before required times are entered, and make the AI analysis resolve or show a useful fallback. A complete saved-shift flow remains unverified.

before.feedback: The accommodation filters and detailed listing views work, and the resident hub gives the concept breadth. Strengthen trust and reliability: every initial listing showed the same 92% match despite budget differences, one image was missing, and the sample agreement audit returned to its ready state without an analysis.

after.feedback: The city filter and detailed property views work, and agreement review and resident services give the concept breadth. But every initial property showed the same 92% fit, the under-₹15,000 action left expensive listings visible, and the sample agreement audit produced no observed result. Make matching and the core audit dependable before claiming verified fit.
